scenes.title: AWS API Gateway
scenes.narration: Amazon API Gateway provides a managed front door for APIs. It receives client requests, matches a route and method, applies the configured security and traffic controls, then forwards to a backend integration such as Lambda or an HTTP service. Distinguish REST, HTTP and WebSocket API types because their features and pricing differ. API Gateway is not the application business logic and does not replace authorization inside downstream systems. For a Bedrock-powered application, an API route can provide a stable client interface while the backend model or orchestration evolves independently. Design limits, timeouts, CORS, logging and error responses together rather than adding them after deployment.  From an architecture perspective, identify which component owns the request, where state is stored, which service performs the work, and how failures are surfaced. In exam scenarios, compare latency, operational effort, least-privilege access and recovery behavior before picking an integration.

scenes.title: API Gateway Integrations: High-Level Overview
scenes.narration: An integration specifies how a request accepted by API Gateway reaches its backend. A Lambda proxy integration passes structured request details to the function and relies on its response contract. HTTP integrations forward to an HTTP endpoint; AWS service integrations can call supported service APIs through configured mapping and credentials. The right choice depends on transformation needs, backend type and whether custom business logic is necessary. Mapping templates or parameter mappings can translate the public API shape into a backend request. Remember that authentication at the API boundary and IAM permission to invoke the target are distinct layers. Trace the request from client to route, authorization, integration and response.  From an architecture perspective, identify which component owns the request, where state is stored, which service performs the work, and how failures are surfaced. In exam scenarios, compare latency, operational effort, least-privilege access and recovery behavior before picking an integration.

scenes.title: API Gateway AWS Service Integration: Kinesis Example
scenes.narration: This pattern connects an API request to a Kinesis stream without inserting a Lambda function for every call. API Gateway can transform the request body into the shape expected by an AWS service integration and invoke the appropriate stream operation using a configured IAM role. The record must include the required stream information, payload encoding and partition-key choice. The stream then decouples ingestion from downstream processing, and consumers can process records later. This is useful for telemetry or application events where the caller needs a quick acceptance response, not immediate analytics. Still protect the API with authentication, throttling, request validation and monitoring, because direct service integration does not automatically make ingestion safe.  From an architecture perspective, identify which component owns the request, where state is stored, which service performs the work, and how failures are surfaced. In exam scenarios, compare latency, operational effort, least-privilege access and recovery behavior before picking an integration.

scenes.title: API Gateway Endpoint Types
scenes.narration: For REST APIs, regional, edge-optimized and private endpoint choices affect how callers reach the API. A regional endpoint is designed for regional clients or your own CloudFront distribution. Edge optimization uses an AWS-managed CloudFront distribution for geographically distributed public clients. Private endpoints limit access through supported VPC endpoint arrangements and policies. Do not confuse endpoint type with authorization: a public endpoint can still require strong identity controls, and a private endpoint still needs carefully scoped policies. HTTP and WebSocket API offerings have different endpoint capabilities, so verify the selected API type before using a REST-specific exam rule. Choose based on caller location, connectivity, security and operations.  From an architecture perspective, identify which component owns the request, where state is stored, which service performs the work, and how failures are surfaced. In exam scenarios, compare latency, operational effort, least-privilege access and recovery behavior before picking an integration.

scenes.title: API Gateway Security
scenes.narration: Protect API Gateway with layered controls, starting with authentication and authorization. Depending on API type and requirements, options include IAM authorization, JWT or Cognito-based authorization and Lambda authorizers. Resource policies, WAF support where applicable, throttling and usage plans can further restrict abusive requests. However, usage plans and API keys alone are not user authentication. Encrypt data in transit, validate inputs, and avoid disclosing secrets through logs or error responses. For a generative AI endpoint, enforce per-user quotas and restrict access to underlying documents and models. A successfully authenticated caller should not automatically be allowed to retrieve every tenant's data or invoke every costly model.  From an architecture perspective, identify which component owns the request, where state is stored, which service performs the work, and how failures are surfaced. In exam scenarios, compare latency, operational effort, least-privilege access and recovery behavior before picking an integration.

scenes.title: API Gateway and Generative AI
scenes.narration: The core architecture is a controlled client-facing API in front of a generative AI workflow. API Gateway accepts a request, checks applicable authorization, then invokes Lambda or another approved backend. The backend can retrieve context, apply policy checks and call Bedrock. API responses need explicit error and timeout behavior because inference can be slower than ordinary database lookups. Consider streaming or asynchronous designs when needed instead of forcing every task through a single synchronous request. Guardrails and content filtering complement, but do not replace, authorization and data minimization. Track latency, model usage, throttling and request costs. Separate user-visible answer generation from background ingestion and indexing so each component scales appropriately.  From an architecture perspective, identify which component owns the request, where state is stored, which service performs the work, and how failures are surfaced. In exam scenarios, compare latency, operational effort, least-privilege access and recovery behavior before picking an integration.

scenes.title: AWS AppConfig
scenes.narration: AWS AppConfig helps teams deploy and validate application configuration without redeploying code for every adjustment. Configuration can be hosted or retrieved from supported sources, validated before rollout and deployed gradually according to a strategy. Applications can use agents or extension patterns to retrieve current values with caching rather than issuing uncontrolled calls. Configuration is different from secrets: sensitive credentials belong in an appropriate secrets-management system. A staged deployment with monitors can limit the impact of a bad feature flag or threshold. Think of AppConfig as a control plane for runtime behavior, while the application still owns the logic that interprets the configuration.  From an architecture perspective, identify which component owns the request, where state is stored, which service performs the work, and how failures are surfaced. In exam scenarios, compare latency, operational effort, least-privilege access and recovery behavior before picking an integration.

scenes.title: AppConfig and Generative AI
scenes.narration: Generative AI applications often need to tune behavior independently of code deployment. AppConfig can distribute feature flags, model-selection preferences, prompt-template identifiers or retrieval thresholds to application components. A gradual rollout lets operators compare latency and quality metrics before all users receive a change. Store secret credentials elsewhere and avoid placing highly sensitive prompt contents in publicly visible configurations. Validate values so an invalid model identifier or unsupported parameter cannot break production requests. Pair configuration deployment with observable alarms and a rollback policy. The point is controlled experimentation: changing a model route or retrieval setting should be reversible and measurable instead of requiring an emergency code release.  From an architecture perspective, identify which component owns the request, where state is stored, which service performs the work, and how failures are surfaced. In exam scenarios, compare latency, operational effort, least-privilege access and recovery behavior before picking an integration.
